questions.question: When is an entire object considered to be floating on water?
options: Only when it is completely out of the water
If any part of it remains above the water's surface
Only when exactly half of it is submerged
When it sinks to the very bottom

questions.question: A student wants to test if a toy boat floats better in a deep swimming pool or a shallow basin of water. How does the depth of the liquid affect how well an object floats?
options: It floats much better in deeper water
It floats much better in shallower water
Floating does not depend on the depth of the liquid
An object can only float if the liquid's depth is twice the object's height

questions.question: Under what condition will an object float in water based on its shape and mass?
options: If its shape can push its own mass of water out of the way without going under
If its shape is perfectly spherical to minimize contact area
If its shape is designed to trap at least half its mass in air
If its shape allows it to absorb water to increase its weight

questions.question: Approximately how much force is required to lift a 1 kg mass vertically upwards on Earth?
options: 1 N

questions.question: If a spring is stretched within its elastic limit, how does its extension change as you add equal increments of force?
options: The extension increases by the same amount for each equal increase in force
The extension increases by doubling for each equal increase in force
The extension increases by smaller and smaller amounts
The extension remains completely constant regardless of force

questions.question: What makes a spring described as an elastic material?
options: It can be stretched to any length without ever breaking
It returns to its original length when the stretching force is removed
It permanently changes its shape after a single force is applied
It increases in temperature whenever it is compressed

questions.question: What is a primary mechanical function of a lever in terms of force?
options: Levers can multiply a small force into a larger force
Levers can eliminate the force of gravity on a load
Levers can convert electrical energy directly into mechanical force
Levers can decrease the force required to keep an object at rest

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the concept of pressure?
options: Pressure is a measure of the total weight of an object
Pressure is a measure of how concentrated a force is
Pressure is a measure of the speed of a moving object
Pressure is a measure of the volume of liquid displaced

questions.question: Which formula is used to calculate pressure?
options: Pressure = force × area
Pressure = force ÷ area
Pressure = mass × area
Pressure = force + area

questions.question: What is another name for the unit of pressure 'newtons per square metre' (N/m²)?
options: The Joule (J)
The Pascal (Pa)
The Watt (W)
The Newton (N)

questions.question: Why does the pressure in a liquid increase as you go deeper?
options: The density of the liquid increases exponentially with depth
There is more liquid above pushing down
The temperature of the liquid decreases with depth
The gravity acting on the liquid increases at the bottom

questions.question: Why does atmospheric pressure reduce with increasing height?
options: The air temperature becomes much hotter at high altitudes
There is less air above pushing down
The Earth's gravity is significantly stronger at high altitudes
The wind speed decreases the density of the air

questions.question: How does the extension of a rubber band behave when you apply equal-sized increases in force?
options: The extension increases by the same amount for each equal increase in force
The extension increases by different amounts for each equal-sized increase in force
The extension does not change at all until the band snaps
The extension decreases with each increase in force

questions.question: What happens to the particles in a floor when a bigger mass is placed on it?
options: They expand and become much less dense
More particles in the floor are squashed together
They begin to slide past each other like a liquid
They are destroyed by the weight of the mass

questions.question: How is the turning effect, or moment, of a force calculated?
options: Moment = force ÷ distance from the pivot
Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = mass × distance from the pivot
Moment = force + distance from the pivot
